title: Is Saturated Fat Unhealthy?
text:
Saturated Fat
Is saturated fat bad for you?

Does reducing dietary saturated fat reduce the occurrence of heart attacks, cardiovascular death, or death by any cause?


What do the latest meta-analyses on RCTs say?



April 2025 meta-analysis said “no”.
December 2025 meta-analysis said “yes…sort of”.



So which is it?

title: Is Saturated Fat Unhealthy?
text:
Meta-anlaysis

A method of combining evidence from similar studies
using quantitative methods (statistical techniques)
More precise conclusion (higher statistical power than a single study)
Studies should be relatively similar in design and outcome
The top of the evidence hierarchy

title: Is Saturated Fat Unhealthy?
text:
Lack of Consistency
Why?



the underlying trials differ in intervention, comparator, replacement nutrient, population, duration, setting, and outcomes
which trials to include and even which version of a trial to include
how the intervention is defined and classified

reducing / replacing saturated fat, PUFA replacement, unsaturated-fat replacement, reduced / modified fat, CHO replacment

how the replacement nutrient is defined and classified
which outcomes are analyzed and how they are classified

MI, CHD death, CVD death, stroke, coronary events, all-cause mortality

how much subgrouping to do

trial length, participant age, risk profile, primary / secondary prevention, dietary replacement

how the trials are pooled and analyzed

fixed vs random effects, subgrouping, reanalyses, treatment of mixed interventions

title: Is Saturated Fat Unhealthy?
text:
Summary


All of these RCTs have significant issues that lead to little confidence in the results in either direction
No more meta-analyses of RCTs on saturated fat and hard cardiovascular or mortality endpoints

If you ever see another meta-analysis on RCTs of saturated fat reduction…

But what do we do? Is SFA good, bad, neutral, it depends?
Can we answer this question?


Where do we go from here?

title: Is Saturated Fat Unhealthy?
text:
Evidence Types


Human hard endpoint RCTs
Mechanistic / biological evidence
Animal experimental evidence
Human surrogate-outcome RCTs
Observational studies

title: Is Saturated Fat Unhealthy?
text:
Conclusion


The RCTs included in these meta-analyses are highly variable and have major problems in design, conduct, and applicability, making the pooled evidence difficult to interpret.
They do not convincingly establish that reducing dietary saturated fat lowers the occurrence of these hard outcomes, or that it does not.
More meta-analyses of RCTs on saturated fat and hard cardiovascular or mortality endpoints won’t help



Perhaps RCTs are a poor test of this hypothesis in practice.
Perhaps our original question was too imprecise.




But what do we do? Is saturated fat good, bad, neutral, it depends?
Can we answer this question?


Where do we go from here?
